ADDED i2: A single NUL (U+0000) character, expressed without an invisible literal.
ADDED i3: Two characters: a NUL (U+0000) followed by 'r'.
ADDED i4: Eighteen NUL (U+0000) characters (a freshly allocated char array is zero-filled).
ADDED i5: The (deprecated) DP length array has dimensions (left.length()+1) x (right.length()+1). For two identical 6-character inputs the outer dimension is therefore 7.
ADDED i6: When one input is empty, the longest common subsequence is the empty string.
ADDED i7: The deprecated (misspelled) overload delegates to longestCommonSubsequence, so an empty input also yields the empty string.
ADDED i8: longestCommonSubsequence rejects a null input with IllegalArgumentException.
ADDED i10: The deprecated overload also rejects null inputs with IllegalArgumentException.
ADDED i12: apply returns the LCS length. NUL_THEN_R shares its single NUL character with a large zero-filled buffer, so the score is 1.
ADDED i13: apply returns 0 when one input is empty (an empty wrapped char array).
ADDED i14: apply returns 0 when both inputs are empty.
ADDED i15: apply with a two-char zero-filled buffer still shares the leading NUL from NUL_THEN_R, giving a score of 1.
ADDED i16: apply rejects a null right input with IllegalArgumentException.
ADDED i18: apply rejects null inputs with IllegalArgumentException.
ADDED i20: The deprecated overload returns the actual subsequence: a two-char zero buffer and NUL_THEN_R share the leading NUL character.
ADDED i21: A zero-filled buffer shares no character with "+*QLyOuk", so the longest common subsequence is empty.
